- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.50), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for risk reversal.
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the 10–15 day horizon after a spike; add 2–5% to forecast for that window.
- Model overestimates in early 30-day forecasts when sentiment is volatile; apply a 1–2% downward adjustment if sentiment swings >0.50 in last 3 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30-day forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- Overshoot after spikes: if model peaks >10% above prior 3-day high, cap forecast at 10% below that peak for next 3 days.
- Sentiment + price divergence: if sentiment >0.67 but price drops >2%, model is overconfident; reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 5 days.
